title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Braiden McGregor (pec) out for season with torn pec
items.desc: Braiden McGregor (pec) is out for the 2026 season with a torn pec.
items.impact: McGregor had racked up eight total tackles on the season before suffering the injury. He had found additional playing time thanks to injuries ahead of him, and now he will be put on the shelf himself. The Jets will be looking for some defensive line help in the next few days.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Pat Bryant (ankle) to miss several weeks with sprained ankle
items.desc: Pat Bryant (ankle) is likely to miss the next several weeks with a sprained ankle.
items.impact: Bryant was carted off the field after suffering the injury, but the good news is that while it will knock him out for a while, it's not overly major. Bryant had three catches on as many targets for 47 yards, leading all Bronco receivers and pass catchers not named RJ Harvey.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Kyle Juszczyk (knee) could miss couple of weeks with knee injury
items.desc: Kyle Juszczyk (knee) could miss a couple of weeks after hyperextending his knee in the Niners game against Denver on Sunday. He will undergo an MRI on Monday.
items.impact: Juszczyk is better known for his blocking and receiving than rushing, and right now is playing just a part-time relief role in the 49ers' offense. His absence could open up some more work for Kaelon Black, but that's unlikely.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Kyle Monangai (thumb) to be evaluated Monday
items.desc: Kyle Monangai (thumb) will be evaluated for a thumb injury on Monday.
items.impact: According to the running back, he looked down at his hand before realizing any pain. His status is up in the air, so fantasy managers will need to monitor the situation as details emerge on whether he will miss time.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Tyson Bagent will start in Week 5 against Green Bay
items.desc: Tyson Bagent will start next week against Green Bay, per Head Coach Ben Johnson.
items.impact: Bagent had himself a nice day against the Jets, even without throwing a touchdown. He simply wasn't asked to do much against a Jets team that lacked any bite. Against the Packers, however, you would expect tougher competition, so Bagent could have a better stat line next week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Will Shipley quiet in loss Sunday
items.desc: Will Shipley rushed the ball six times for 23 yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Shipley saw six touches on Sunday, but he was only able to turn them into 23 yards against the Rams, which left him with a poor fantasy total. He may see more work than usual moving forward if starter Saquon Barkley has to miss time with his hamstring injury.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Eagles D/ST logs two interceptions Sunday
items.desc: The Eagles' D/ST logged two interceptions and one sack while allowing 24 points in Sunday's loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Philadelphia's defense had an up-and-down game on Sunday. They logged two interceptions and didn't allow Matthew Stafford to score a single touchdown through the air, but they allowed three on the ground and allowed Los Angeles to put up 24 points en route to a win on the road. This unit should only be started in favorable matchups moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jake Elliott perfect in loss Sunday
items.desc: Jake Elliott went 2-for-2 on his field-goal attempts and 2-for-2 on his extra-point attempts in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Elliott looked good on Sunday. He made all four of his attempted kicks against the Rams, including an impressive field goal from 56 yards out. He should continue to be an okay fantasy option moving forward, though Philadelphia may not be in scoring range as much as usual if Saquon Barkley (hamstring) misses any time.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Darius Cooper hauls in two touchdowns in loss Sunday
items.desc: Darius Cooper hauled in 3-of-7 targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Cooper was one of the lone bright spots on Philadelphia's offense on Sunday. He caught both of the team's passing touchdowns against the Rams, although he was only able to rack up 33 yards in the process. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to be a good fantasy option moving forward, however, especially with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) set to make his return to the lineup at some point.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Zach Ertz held to 13 yards Sunday
items.desc: Zach Ertz caught 2-of-4 targets for just 13 yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: The veteran tight end saw more work than usual in Week 4 with Dallas Goedert (knee) still out of the lineup for the Eagles. Ertz wasn't able to do much himself, catching just two passes for 13 yards against the Rams. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect much out of him for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tank Bigsby leads team in rushing Sunday
items.desc: Tank Bigsby rushed the ball 14 times for 55 yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Bigsby stepped up on Sunday and took over as the team's top running back when Saquon Barkley left the game with a hamstring injury. He did okay in the absence of the veteran, though he left something to be desired with his efficiency and involvement in the passing game. He could be a big-time waiver pickup this week if the Eagles don't get good news regarding the severity of Barkley's injury.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Makai Lemon underwhelming in loss Sunday
items.desc: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-6 targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) was sidelined for the Eagles on Sunday, but the rookie still wasn't able to take advantage and ended up with just three catches for 27 yards against the Rams. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect much value out of Lemon for the foreseeable future after his slow start to the season.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jaylin Lane (ankle) likely done for 2026 season
items.desc: Jaylin Lane (ankle) is likely out for the rest of the 2026 season after suffering a fracture and dislocation of his ankle.
items.impact: Lane was not heavily involved in the rotation at reciever, but he still provided depth and an explosive play option. The team will now look to bring someone in to help with depth and punt return duties.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Dontayvion Wicks disappoints in loss Sunday
items.desc: Dontayvion Wicks caught 3-of-5 targets for just 18 yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Wicks wasn't able to get much going on Sunday. He finished with just 18 yards through the air against the Rams, which of course left him with a poor fantasy total. He should bounce back sometime in the near future, though a big part of his outlook will also depend on the health of Devonta Smith (hamstring) moving forward.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Tyreek Hill expected to sign in the coming days
items.desc: Tyreek Hill is expected to sign with a team in the coming days, per his agent. He's been linked to the Chiefs, but other teams are in the mix.
items.impact: Hill could give the Chiefs some depth, but it will be interesting to see how much of an impact he could make at this stage of his career while also coming off of a major knee injury. He's worth stashing, but keep expectations low.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Saquon Barkley suffers hamstring injury Sunday
items.desc: Saquon Barkley rushed the ball two times for eight yards and caught one pass for two yards before leaving Sunday's loss to the Rams with a hamstring injury.
items.impact: Barkley suffered a hamstring injury during Sunday's loss to the Rams. The severity of the injury is unknown at this point, so fantasy managers should keep close tabs on updates about his status throughout the week. Tank Bigsby will be primed for more work if the veteran has to miss any time.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jalen Hurts totals 111 yards in loss Sunday
items.desc: Jalen Hurts completed 12-of-27 passing attempts for 93 yards and two touchdowns while adding 18 yards on the ground in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Hurts didn't play well on Sunday. He completed less than half of his passing attempts against the Rams and finished with just 93 passing yards, though he was still able to pick up two touchdowns through the air. He will continue to be underwhelming until DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is back in the lineup for the Eagles.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Rams D/ST allows 20 points Sunday
items.desc: The Rams' D/ST logged four sacks and allowed 20 points in Sunday's win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
items.impact: Los Angeles' had a decent performance in Week 4, but they weren't able to log any turnovers, which hurt their final fantasy score. This is a strong unit but shouldn't be started in next week's tough matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Harrison Mevis misses kick in win Sunday
items.desc: Harrison Mevis went 3-for-3 on his extra-point attempts and 1-for-2 on his field-goal attempts in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
items.impact: Mevis made four out of his five kicks on Sunday but missed one field-goal attempt against the Eagles. Luckily, the Rams were still able to pick up the win on the road, and fantasy managers should continue to regard him as a worthwhile option moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Konata Mumpfield quiet in win Sunday
items.desc: Konata Mumpfield caught 1-of-3 targets for seven yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
items.impact: Mumpfield wasn't able to get much going on Sunday, finishing with just one catch for seven yards in a win over the Eagles. He isn't expected to play a big role for the Rams moving forward now that Puka Nacua is healthy and back in the lineup.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tyler Higbee solid in win Sunday
items.desc: Tyler Higbee hauled in 5-of-6 targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
items.impact: The veteran tight end stepped up and played a bigger role again in Week 4. He did well with his opportunities, finishing with five catches for 67 yards in a win over the Eagles. He should continue to be a viable fantasy option with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) set to be sidelined for a few more weeks at least.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Blake Corum a non-factor in win Sunday
items.desc: Blake Corum rushed the ball five times for 14 yards and caught one pass for seven yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
items.impact: Corum didn't play much of a role for the Rams in Week 4. He saw just six touches over the course of the game and was only able to turn them into 21 yards, as opposed to Kyren Williams' 26 touches for 147 yards. Fantasy managers shouldn't have much hope for Corum to have standalone value anytime soon.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Davante Adams disappoints in win Sunday
items.desc: Davante Adams hauled in 4-of-9 targets for just 32 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
items.impact: Adams was red-hot coming into this game, but he disappointed against the Eagles by catching just four of his nine targets for a measly 32 yards. He is no longer the top wideout on the team with Puka Nacua back in the lineup and healthy, so he will likely revert to being a boom-or-bust fantasy option on a week-to-week basis moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Puka Nacua stellar in return game Sunday
items.desc: Puka Nacua caught 9-of-12 targets for 125 yards and added one touchdown on the ground in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
items.impact: The star wideout made his return to the lineup in Week 4 after missing a bit of time due to an injury of some kind. He looked great in his first game back, finishing with 125 receiving yards and a rushing touchdown in a narrow win over the Eagles. He will continue to be a must-start fantasy option moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kyren Williams dominant in win Sunday
items.desc: Kyren Williams rushed the ball 16 times for 80 yards and two touchdowns and caught 10-of-13 targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
items.impact: Williams had a stellar game in Week 4. He led team with 80 rushing yards, found the end zone two different times, and caught ten passes for 67 yards through the air in Sunday's win over the Eagles. Fantasy managers should be well pleased with this performance and with the fact that he has entirely pulled ahead of Blake Corum in terms of touches in close matchups.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: The Lions D/ST gives up 32 points in Week 4 loss
items.desc: The Lions' defense allowed 32 points on 445 yards of offense in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
items.impact: The Lions' pass rush did at least come up with three sacks on Sunday night. The Detroit defense as a whole, however, was lit up for more than 30-plus points for the third time in four games this season. The Panthers had success through the air (318 yards) and on the ground (127 yards), as the Lions allowed four touchdowns and a couple of field goals. The Lions have registered 15 sacks through four weeks, but that's about the extent of the positives from this unit.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Matthew Stafford doesn't score in win Sunday
items.desc: Matthew Stafford completed 32-of-51 passing attempts for 317 yards and two interceptions in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
items.impact: Stafford was able to lead the Rams to a win on Sunday, but he wasn't able to find a lot of personal success in the process. He failed to score even a single touchdown in this matchup, and he also threw two interceptions, which left him with a poor fantasy total. He should bounce back and return to form sometime in the near future, however,

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Jake Bates nails four field goals in Week 4 loss
items.desc: Jake Bates made all four of his field-goal attempts and both PATs in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
items.impact: Bates put a total of 14 points on the board Sunday night, getting four field-goal tries, as the Lions' offense had trouble finishing drives in the end zone. Bates has yet to miss any of his seven FG attempts or 14 PATs through four games. He's a great fantasy option with the Lions' high-powered offense.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Sam LaPorta hits paydirt in Sunday's loss
items.desc: Sam LaPorta caught 8-of-13 targets for 84 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
items.impact: LaPorta put up new season highs in receptions and yards Sunday night, tying for the team lead with eight grabs. LaPorta also scored for the second time this season. He's not a sure thing every week, but LaPorta is a definite top-10 TE with top-five upside the rest of the way.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown makes eight grabs in Week 4 loss
items.desc: Amon Ra St. Brown came up with 8-of-11 targets for 75 yards in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
items.impact: St. Brown failed to make it four straight games with a touchdown to start the season, but he still produced a solid showing. St. Brown has largely delivered for fantasy managers over the first quarter of the season, averaging nearly eight receptions for more than 75 yards with five scores to this point. He remains a certain WR1.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Isaac TeSlaa approaches 100 yards on Sunday night
items.desc: Isaac TeSlaa hauled in 4-of-8 targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
items.impact: TeSlaa had his biggest game of the season so far Sunday night, and has been showing off his big-play ability over the last two games. Over the past two Sundays, the second-year receiver has brought down seven passes for an average of 23.0 yards per catch. TeSlaa has certainly entered the flex conversation as a boom-or-bust option heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Cardinals.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Jameson Williams clears 100 yards in Week 4 loss
items.desc: Jameson Williams came up with 6-of-8 targets for 102 yards in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
items.impact: After being held under 50 yards and no more than four grabs over the first three weeks of the season, Williams finally got going Sunday night. The big-play blazer had a long gain of 49 yards and averaged 17 yards on his half-dozen receptions. Williams should be viewed as an upside WR3 heading into Week 5.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Jahmyr Gibbs finds the end zone in Week 4
items.desc: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 46 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries, adding 31 yards on four catches in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
items.impact: Gibbs was limited to a season-low 77 yards of offense Sunday, but he still found the end zone for the seventh time in four weeks. The Panthers' defense did a solid job of holding Gibbs to 3.1 yards per carry and another season-low of four receptions. Still, the dynamic back remains an elite, dual-threat option heading to Arizona in Week 5.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Jared Goff airs it out for 412 yards in Sunday night's loss
items.desc: Jared Goff completed 32 of 52 passes for 412 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
items.impact: Through Sunday, Goff now holds the NFL's highest single-game total in passing yards for the season. The Lions threw the ball 52 times compared to just 15 runs, leading to Goff's seventh career 400-yard passing performance. Surprisingly, the Lions' QB only connected for one touchdown pass on the night. Overall, Goff has been excellent through four weeks, completing 67.7% of his throws for better than 300 yards per game with a 9-0 TD/INT ratio.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) still 'weeks away' from return
items.desc: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is still considered "weeks away" from returning from IR due to his hamstring injury, despite being eligible to return at the conclusion of Week 4. It appears Week 7 is the earliest we could see him return, but the Saints bye is the following week, so Week 9 is sounding more realistic.
items.impact: It's a tough blow for Tyson's stock and for fantasy managers who have held on to him this long. Tyson has loads of promise and could unlock something for a Saints offense that's already looking good. However, we will have to wait several more weeks to see him on the field, and in his absence, Juwan Johnson and Devaughn Vele will continue to be viable starts.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Bryce Young picks apart Detroit pass defense in Week 4
items.desc: Bryce Young completed 29 of 41 passes for 329 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
items.impact: Young cleared 300 yards passing for the second time this season on Sunday night and has thrown for a minimum of 287 through four weeks. The 25-year-old QB certainly seems to have stepped up to a new level. Through Sunday, he leads the league in passing yards, with a 62.3% completion rate and 9-2 TD/INT ratio. The Panthers are off in Week 5, but Young should be viewed among the QB1 ranks most weeks after that.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Dolphins D/ST logs four sacks Sunday
items.desc: The Dolphins' D/ST logged four sacks and allowed 15 points in Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Miami's defense didn't play bad on Sunday. They were able to get to the quarterback four times and only allowed 15 points, though their offense still wasn't able to beat out that number. This unit should not be started moving forward, however, especially in a matchup against the Bengals next week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Riley Patterson perfect in loss Sunday
items.desc: Riley Patterson made his lone field-goal attempt and his lone extra-point attempt in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Patterson played well enough on Sunday, making both of his relatively easy kicks in a loss to the Vikings. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high hopes for him moving forward, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Greg Dulcich doesn't catch pass Sunday
items.desc: Greg Dulcich did not record a single target or touch in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: The veteran was a complete non-factor on Sunday. He didn't log a single target or touch against the Vikings, which was rather surprising after he caught five passes last week. He remains off of the fantasy radar moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Chris Bell catchless in loss Sunday
items.desc: Chris Bell did not bring in any of his three targets in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: The rookie had one big touchdown that got called back due to penalty, and outside of that, he wasn't able to do anything at all. He didn't catch any of his three targets and ended up with a goose egg for fantasy purposes. He should not be started moving forward, even if he has enough talent to break out at some point in the season.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Chuba Hubbard delivers big performance Sunday night
items.desc: Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
items.impact: The Lions' defense could not stop the pass or the run Sunday night. Hubbard turned in his highest rushing total since December 2024 in this contest. The 27-year-old back has now gained more than 200 yards on 39 carries over the last two weeks, proving himself capable of being a workhorse back yet again. Hubbard will return to the field for a matchup with the Eagles in Week 6.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jaylen Wright quiet in loss Sunday
items.desc: Jaylen Wright carried the ball five times for seven yards in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Wright didn't see a large workload on Sunday. He finished with just five carries for seven yards against the Vikings, and he wasn't able to get involved in the passing game either. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high expectations for him moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ollie Gordon II plays well in loss Sunday
items.desc: Ollie Gordon II rushed the ball nine times for 100 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Gordon was one of the only bright spots for Miami's offense this week. He finished with 100 yards and a touchdown on just nine carries, which left him with a great efficiency number in this game. He has clearly separated himself from Jaylen Wright in terms of talent and output, but they continue to be somewhat close together in terms of opportunities, which could limit Gordon moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Malik Washington leads team in receiving Sunday
items.desc: Malik Washington caught five passes for 67 yards in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Washington played pretty well on Sunday, finishing with most of the team's receiving yards in their loss to the Vikings. He's one of their only competent receivers at this point, but he still shouldn't be started in most league formats for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: John Metchie III hauls in three passes in Week 4
items.desc: John Metchie III caught 3-of-5 passes for 37 yards in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
items.impact: With Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee) out, Metchie certainly seemed like the WR2 for the Panthers. Still, that was a distant No. 2 behind Tetairoa McMillan. Metchie has now come up with 5-of-10 targets for 56 yards and a score over the last two games. Coker should return after the Panthers' Week 6 bye, so Metchie should be left on the waiver wire.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Malik Willis totals under 100 yards in loss Sunday
items.desc: Malik Willis completed 9-of-17 passing attempts for 85 yards and added 11 yards on the ground in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Willis wasn't able to get anything going on Sunday. He finished with just 96 total yards over the course of the afternoon, and he wasn't able to score either and lost a fumble, which left him with a terrible fantasy total. Nobody outside of Ollie Gordon II should be started on this offense moving forward.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Brycen Tremayne catches a pair of passes in Week 4
items.desc: Brycen Tremayne secured 2-of-3 targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
items.impact: After leading the Panthers in receiving yards in Week 3, Tremayne put up just modest numbers Sunday night. He was involved in the passing game, but even with fellow WRs Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee) out, Tremayne finished fifth in targets for the Panthers.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Vikings D/ST plays well in win Sunday
items.desc: The Vikings' D/ST logged two sacks and a fumble recovery while allowing ten points in Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: Minnesota's defense capitalized on a good matchup on Sunday. They logged a few big plays to help out their offense and held Miami to just ten points over the course of the game. This unit is one of the NFL's finest and should continue to be started in most matchups moving forward.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Tetairoa McMillan shreds Lions secondary Sunday night
items.desc: Tetairoa McMillan collected 14 receptions on 16 targets for 192 yards and a pair of touchdowns in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
items.impact: For those frustrated by McMillan's paltry output in Week 3, the second-year star erupted for career highs in receptions and yards Sunday night. He also recorded the second multi-touchdown game of his career. It's important to note that this performance came with both Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee) out, but McMillan still displayed his immense upside. He's a solid WR2 for fantasy purposes at present.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Will Reichard scores 15 points in win Sunday
items.desc: Will Reichard made all five of his field-goal attempts in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: Reichard had a great game on Sunday, being responsible for all 15 of Minnesota's points in their close win over the Dolphins. He should continue to be a viable fantasy asset for the foreseeable future.
